value:
Unparseable store files (#215 step 1): src/utils/unreadable.ts is the vocabulary (StoreUnreadableError, code STORE_UNREADABLE, messages, the bootstrap block) and holds the registry listUnreadableFiles(). directoryStore.ts detects; storage.ts, both wrappers (instrumentation.ts, mcp-server.ts), context.ts, lint.ts and confirm.ts surface.

GOTCHAS:
- listUnreadableFiles lives in unreadable.ts, fed by registerUnreadableSource from store.ts, NOT exported from store.ts: ~10 suites vi.mock('../store') with explicit factories, and a new named export there fails them at link time ("Export named ... not found").
- It does no I/O: it reports what scans this process already ran. That is nearly every command, because resolveKey loads the alias map, which scans both stores.
- Write guards read the target file fresh (probeEntryFile / readSidecar) — scanAndSync fast-skips on an unchanged directory mtime.
- storage.ts getValue/setValue wrap the fast path in a catch-all that falls through; the typed error must be rethrown there or get becomes "not found" and set falls into save().
- save() throws after the odd epoch bump, so it writes the even epoch back first. setOne reads the existing file BEFORE the bump.
- A destination pre-read (set/copy/rename) uses getValueForWrite so the message is the refused write, not a failed read.
- save() is called once per FILE, so its guard is per save, not per command: `set k v -a alias` wrote the value before the alias map refused. Multi-file commands (set -a/--confirm, rename, rm; CLI and MCP) call assertSidecarsWritable BEFORE their first write. It takes a resolver callback and steps aside if that throws, so PROJECT_UNRESOLVED stays the error.
- hasConfirm stays LITERAL. The run gates add confirmListUnreadable() to fail closed; rename uses hasConfirm to decide whether to move a flag, and a fail-closed 'yes' there made it write the conflicted list after the value had moved.
- New exports go in unreadable.ts for the same reason as the registry: '../alias', '../confirm', '../storage' and '../store' are all vi.mock'ed with explicit factories somewhere. mcp-server.ts may only import names those mocks already have.
- Classify conflict vs parse only AFTER JSON.parse fails: a valid value can contain marker lines.
- scanAndSync fast-skips on an unchanged directory mtime, and a repair by editor save or `cp` does not move it. unreadableFileChanged() re-stats the files recorded as unreadable before the skip. Without it the long-lived MCP server kept the entry out of load(), and its next full save DELETED the repaired file: save() rescans under the lock (its own epoch write moves the directory), re-reads the file, and finds it missing from the data being saved. An in-place BREAK of a healthy file is still invisible until the directory moves; single-key get/set read fresh.
- getValueForWrite is readForWrite: on an unreadable hit it asks again in the write's own store, so a broken GLOBAL file does not block a project write. The healthy lookup is unchanged — a global-only value still counts as "already exists". mcp-server.ts calls readForWrite itself; never import getValueForWrite there (mocked '../storage').
- assertSubtreeReadable runs BEFORE the existence lookup in rm/rename: a parent whose only child is unreadable looks absent.
- save() step 3c refuses a write to an ancestor or descendant of an unreadable entry (nameCollisionError). setOne sends those to save() by returning false on the file-name collision.
- removeAlias / renameAlias / removeConfirm assert their sidecar. The cascade helpers (removeAliasesForKey, removeConfirmForKey) do not — their callers pre-flight.
- MCP: setAbsoluteDisplayPaths(true) at startup, because the server's cwd is not the project; and a StoreUnreadableError renders as TWO blocks (message, then JSON code + files), so an error result has 2 blocks plus any warnings.
- Tests: callMcpTool spawns a server per call; withMcpSession (mcp-integration.test.ts) keeps one alive across calls. To exercise the fast skip, pin the directory mtime in WHOLE seconds — a Date or a fractional utimes value does not round-trip to the cached mtimeMs, the skip never applies, and the test passes without the fix.

KNOWN GAPS, filed as #270 (deferred past 1.4.0): with an unreadable alias map, `set <alias>` creates an entry named after the alias (not destructive); `data reset` leaves unreadable files in place; a merely invalid file has no supported removal — rm refuses it, the message says delete it by hand; a long-lived MCP server misses an in-place break. One full-suite run stalled with no output during this work and never reproduced — cause unknown.

SINCE #254/#262 (2026-11-26): every write is an update() transaction (see [[arch.storeTransactions]]); where this entry says save(), read update(). Every exit from a commit writes the even epoch back.
